assertions.text: Negative rate is rejected — a rejection row with an expected-exception column.

assertions.text: Negative hours must be shown, not silently chosen. The solution commits to one semantics and makes it visible as an example row.

assertions.text: Reference valid rows use blank cells (not 0) when a band is not exercised, requiring Integer parameters not int.
assertions.evidence: All hour parameters are declared as 'double' (e.g., 'double weekdayHours', 'double sundayHours'). Rows use explicit 0 values instead of blank cells. No Integer parameters or @TypeConverter visible to handle null→0 conversion.

assertions.text: Scenario names describe work patterns (e.g. 'Part-time', 'Five hours overtime', 'Full Sunday shift') — not 'Test case 1' or expected outcomes
assertions.evidence: Hours below the overtime threshold, Just past the overtime threshold, Week with overtime, Sunday, and holiday hours

assertions.text: Arithmetic must be internally consistent with the rule the rows state.

assertions.evidence: Zero rate appears only once in end-to-end table: 'Zero hourly rate is allowed | 40 | 5 | 0 | 0.00 | 0.00'. Not a value set across multiple hour shapes; only one scenario at rate 0.

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Zero rate is allowed and yields zero pay for any hours — make it a row, ideally a value set over several hour shapes at rate 0.
assertions.evidence: End-to-end table includes 'Zero hourly rate is allowed | 40 | 5 | 0 | 0.00 | 0.00' showing zero rate with mixed hours yields zero pay.

assertions.text: The test method body contains no if/ternary null-handling or parsing logic. Null-to-default conversion (e.g. blank Sunday hours → 0) is handled via a @TypeConverter method or a private helper, keeping the test method limited to arrange/act/assert.
assertions.evidence: All test methods contain only assertEquals/assertThrows calls with no if/ternary logic. No null-handling visible in method bodies.

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Weekday hours', 'Sunday hours', 'Hourly rate', 'Weekly pay?') — not implementation terms like 'weekdayHrs', 'int', 'param1'.
assertions.evidence: Column headers use 'Weekday Hours', 'Sunday Hours', 'Holiday Hours', 'Hourly Rate', 'Total Pay?' — all business language. However, method parameters use camelCase implementation terms: 'weekdayHours', 'hourlyRate', 'weekdayPay' instead of matching the column names exactly.

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
assertions.evidence: Five separate @TableTest methods: weekday pay, premium pay, combine+floor, negative-rate rejection, and end-to-end integration. Each addresses a distinct concern.

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer rows per table is expected when concerns are properly separated.
assertions.evidence: Weekday table: 7 rows (boundary cases at 40/41, different rates, negative). Premium table: 6 rows (Sunday only, holiday only, combined, negative). Combine table: 6 rows. No cross-product permutations.

assertions.text: Payable hours categorisation (1x regular, 1.5x overtime, 2x Sunday/holiday) and pay calculation (hours × rate) are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: The tables do not separate classification from calculation. Each row shows hours and rate together, computing pay directly. There is no table showing '41 weekday hours → 40 regular + 1 overtime' as a classification step separate from the pay arithmetic.
